text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: spike in gateway 5xx (segfaults) — runtime service 'model-runner-01' reporting SIGSEGVs and OOMs across multiple hosts. error rate ~18% on /v1/generate over last 2m. paging maya (on-call).

maya: seeing the alerts. pulling traces now, joining incident channel.

raj: FYI support is getting inbound tickets about timeouts. customer-impact looks like a handful of high-traffic customers affected.

maya: quick snapshot — rolling 5xx across three AZs. kernel messages show repeated `segfault at 0 ip` on `infer_runner` process. attaching log snippet:```
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] infer_runner[pid=2345] SIGSEGV pc=0x7f8b1c2a addr=0x0
Backtrace: 0x7f8b1c2a 0x7f8b3d0c ...
```

sam: can we reroute traffic to the fallback model pool? policy should allow immediate shift.

eng-runtime: triggering reroute now. running:`rctl set-route --service model-infer --policy fallback-variant --weight 100 --dry=false`

maya: applied, seeing traffic drop on affected hosts. overall 5xx down to ~4% but still getting new SIGSEGVs on older nodes.

taylor: starting canary hotfix build with additional null-checks and guard for KV cache access. will push to 5% first.

maya: also scaling up dedicated pool to absorb load: `autoscale up --pool dedicated-gpu --count 6` — gives breathing room for canary.

support-lead: I've messaged the top 10 customers impacted and opened priority support threads. drafting status note for internal comms.

raj: logs also show OOMs on smaller instance types when sequence length spikes. may need to enforce max tokens for in-flight requests as temporary mitigation.

maya: temporary throttle applied at gateway for requests > 4096 tokens. config: `gateway.cfg -> max_input_tokens: 4096`

eng-runtime: canary at 5% is green for 7 minutes, no segfaults. proceeding to 25% rollout. monitoring core dump collection path: `/var/crash/infer_runner/*.core`. please tar and upload to s3: `tar czf /tmp/cores-1789992222.tgz /var/crash/infer_runner && aws s3 cp /tmp/cores-1789992222.tgz s3://redwood-incidents/1789992222/`

maya: collecting cores now. starting postmortem tracking doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-178999 (internal).

eng-runtime: after 25% rollout stable for 12m. pushing to 100% in 2m if no regressions. ETA full rollforward 15m.

support-lead: updating customers — letting them know we've rerouted to fallback and are rolling hotfix. no sustained data loss; some requests retried.

on-technical note from maya: prioritize reproducibility steps — we have two hosts consistently reproducing with same workload, will attach minimal repro.

maya: handing off to oncall-rotation (overnight). next steps for oncall: monitor for residual segfaults, verify core uploads complete, validate no backend regressions, confirm status page update if impact persists >30m.

oncall-rotation: acknowledged. will watch through midnight and escalate to eng-runtime if rate >5% again. :thumbsup:

maya: incident status — mitigated, partial customer impact, hotfix rolled, fallback routing active, cores collected. creating follow-up postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to SEV2 at 2026-03-17T14:10:05Z.
